HubSpot documents this explicitly for the single-send API: > *"Information passed via the v3 or v4 single send APIs will not function within `if` statements, as the templates compile before the information populates."* The template compiles first, then the payload arrives — so `{% if custom.is_member %}` always evaluates against nothing and takes the same branch for everyone. ## What works **The order total** prints normally: ```hubl

Order total: {{ custom.order_total }}

Your exclusive member benefit...
{% endif %} ``` The template compiles against a known contact, so `contact.is_member` resolves. ### 2. Smart content keyed on list membership Add members to a list, use a smart content rule in the template that shows the block only to contacts on that list. This is a UI rule set, not HubL — configure it in the module or template editor under **Smart content**. ### 3. Two templates One for members, one for non-members. Route the API call to the correct template based on `is_member` in your backend logic before the send. ## Which to choose If you are already updating the contact record with order data, option 1 is the cleanest — `is_member` becomes another contact property and the template stays self-contained.
